Performers
Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London (orchestra), Artur Rodzinski (conductor) Documented

Original sleeve and labels establish the displayed credit. Later Westminster reissue documentation and the publisher’s discography identify the orchestra as the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra. That cross-identification is not substituted silently for the original label credit; individual players and soloists are not established.

[2] [1] [4] [15] [5]
Work version
Finale with a reported 37-bar performance cut; supplied digital track presented intact Documented

The cut is explicitly reported for the Westminster performance by the cited discographic review. Its exact bars and position in this transfer are not established. The historical full score is uncut; no missing passage is silently supplied, no alternative performance is substituted, and no local audio edit is made. Exact performing edition remains unknown.

[9] [6] [8]
Recorded
1954-10-02 to 1954-10-14 Inferred, not documented

CiNii’s record for Westminster MVCW-18008 explicitly gives this range; the publisher independently lists the Rodzinski/Royal Philharmonic recording as 1954. Applying those reissue data to this differently credited LP is an inference. No original session ledger or precise movement-by-movement day has been located. 1956 is the selected LP’s publication year, not an invented session date.

[4] [5] [2]
Place
Walthamstow Hall, London Inferred, not documented

Venue transcribed exactly from the reissue catalogue record. The original LP does not supply a venue. Its linkage to the selected LP is the same qualified inference as the session-date attribution; no more specific hall name is invented.

[4]
Label
Westminster Documented

Original sleeve and labels; commercially issued Vinyl LP, Made in U.S.A. Sleeve ©1956 Westminster Recording Sales Corp.

[2] [1]
Catalogue
WN 18001 (disc labels); XWN 18001 (sleeve) Documented

Both forms are visually present on the source object. These identify the selected 1956 issue, not an asserted first edition worldwide. The publisher lists an earlier 1955 Nixa issue of the attributed 1954 performance.

[2] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 2: XTV 22721; movement 2 on that side Documented

Label matrix is legible in the scan. Side 1 contains Moderato/Allegretto; side 2 contains Largo/Allegro non troppo. Take numbers and faint runout/stamper suffixes are unknown and are not guessed.

[2] [3]
Transfer
Internet Archive Documented

The explicit ripping_operator field is credited, not the different uploader/cataloguing operator. A separately named restoration engineer and original recording engineer are unknown.

[1]
Transfer date
2021-09-15 Documented

Derived from the explicit ripping_date field 20210915005548. This is not inferred from publicdate, scandate, addeddate or a later derivative timestamp; timezone is unspecified.

[1]
Processing
LP transfer: Technics SL1200MK5 / Audio-⁠Technica AT95e → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; ArchiveCD 2.2.57lp; source-side 24-bit FLAC and Internet Archive VBR MP3 derivatives Documented

Hardware lineage and ripping software are explicit metadata. Original side FLAC tags say Processed by SoX; exact filtering, declicking, gain, speed calibration and derivative segmentation parameters are unknown. The sleeve’s Panorthophonic tape-recording and RIAA-mastering statements concern the original production, not a modern restoration recipe. No local speed correction, normalization, splice or replacement audio was applied.

[1] [3] [2]
Composition rights
Not cleared as public domain in the EU or US; composition rights remain separate from the historic recording basis Inferred, not documented

Shostakovich died in 1975. The ordinary EU life-plus-70 calculation runs through 2045; this is not a global clearance or a statement of a US expiry date. IMSLP identifies the work as non-public-domain in the EU and US. The inspected score is territorially hosted as public domain in Taiwan and is cited, not republished. No composition licence is asserted.

[11] [14] [7]
Recording rights
Rule 3: territorial EU historic-recording basis; commercial circulation documented by December 1955, selected LP issue dated 1956 Documented

The original Westminster sleeve/labels and album metadata establish the selected 1956 WN 18001/XWN 18001 issue. A visually inspected High Fidelity review, December 1955, p. 80, already names this London orchestra, Rodzinski, his second recording of the Fifth and Westminster catalogue 18001; the review prints SWN 18001 and erroneously calls the symphony D major, so those details are not silently normalized. The publisher also lists Nixa WLP 20004 in 1955. First lawful publication anywhere before 1963 is the rule; no EU-first-release claim is required or made. source.rights.published 1956 remains a conservative upper bound tied to the selected physical issue, not a first-release date. Even using 1956, the ordinary 50-year recording term had expired before the 2013 extension. US sound-recording status is not established. Complete item metadata, original side-transfer provenance and scans disclose no Creative Commons non-commercial condition or separate upstream digital source. This is not a worldwide public-domain or composition-rights clearance.

Shostakovich, Symphony No. 5 in D minor, Op. 47, IV. Allegro non troppo — Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London, Artur Rodzinski. Westminster WN 18001/XWN 18001, issued 1956; side 2, XTV 22721. Session attributed by reissue documentation to 2–⁠14 October 1954, Walthamstow Hall, London. Internet Archive LP transfer, 15 September 2021. Territorial EU recording basis only; US status and composition clearance not established. Finale includes a reported 37-bar performance cut. Rights statement

  1. Internet Archive — complete Westminster album metadata — Complete metadata and files: publication date 1956; US; Westminster WN 18001/XWN 18001; Vinyl LP; explicit ripping_date, ripping_operator and hardware lineage; original side FLACs and individual VBR MP3 derivatives. No licenseurl or non-commercial condition is present.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Westminster WN 18001 / XWN 18001 — original sleeve and labels — Four-page scan visually inspected. PDF p. 2: XWN 18001, ©1956 Westminster Recording Sales Corp., Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London/Artur Rodzinski, Peter Hugh Reed notes, tape recording by Panorthophonic technique and RIAA mastering. P. 3: WN 18001, side 1, XTV 22720. P. 4: WN 18001, side 2, XTV 22721; Made in U.S.A. Faint runout suffixes are not transcribed.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Internet Archive — disc and track metadata — Album dated 1956; side 1 tracks Moderato/Allegretto, side 2 tracks Largo/Allegro Non Troppo. The four selected files are tracks from this source LP, not alternative performances.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. CiNii Books — Westminster MVCW-18008, Symphony No. 5 — 1997 CD catalogue record, Royal Philharmonic Orchestra/Artur Rodzinski. Note: Recorded October 2 to 14, 1954, Walthamstow Hall, London. These are reissue-session data; the link to the differently named original LP orchestra is inferential, not a session ledger reproduced on the LP.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. DSCH Publishers — Symphony No. 5, Op. 47: history and discography — Composition 1937; premiere 21 November 1937, Leningrad Philharmonic Orchestra/Mravinsky; first score publication 1939; contemporary reception documents; introduction to the 1956 score. Discography lists Rodzinski/Royal Philharmonic, 1954, Nixa WLP 20004, mono, 1955. The latter is an earlier-publication lead, not needed to establish the documented 1956 upper bound for the selected LP.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. DSCH Publishers — New Collected Works, volume 5 editorial account — Instrumentation and historical score editions (1939, 1947, 1956, 1961); manuscript not located; uncertainty about authorial sanction for some 1961 changes. Does not identify Rodzinski’s performing edition.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. IMSLP — Symphony No. 5, Op. 47, historical full-score catalogue — Historical full score, item 1014274, Muzgiz plate M. 16313 Г, circa 1939, Edition Musicus reprint. PML-Asia territorial public-domain hosting; the catalogue marks the work non-public-domain in Canada, the US and the EU. No score file is republished by this package.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. Symphony No. 5 — inspected historical full score — Printed pp. 109–⁠165; PDF pp. 111–⁠167. 170-page PDF; printed pages are PDF page minus two. Relevant pages were visually inspected for orchestration. This source is a historical score witness, not proof of the exact performing edition or a bar-aligned transcript of the cut finale.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. Niek Nelissen — Artur Rodzinski, Complete Westminster Recordings — OpusKlassiek, August 2026, Eloquence 484 8489 review. Early paragraph specifies a 37-bar cut in the 1942 Fifth finale; the later Westminster paragraph explicitly states that Rodzinski made the same cut. This supports a reported version difference, not the exact omitted bars or the splice time in this transfer.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  10. Museum collection — Pravda, “Muddle Instead of Music,” 28 January 1936 — Catalogue of the surviving printed clipping of “Сумбур вместо музыки,” Pravda, 28 January 1936, inventory КП 317996/1315. Establishes the dated public attack, not a decoded political programme for individual notes.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  11. Harlow Robinson — Boston Symphony Orchestra work note — Used for Shostakovich’s dates (1906–⁠1975) and the first American performance, Rodzinski/NBC Symphony broadcast, 9 April 1938. The note’s broader interpretive narrative is not treated as proof of private intentions.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  12. Testimony — publication and authenticity controversy — 1979 publication by Solomon Volkov, and summary/bibliography of the authenticity dispute, including Laurel Fay. Used only to identify the disputed status of the memoir claim, not as authentication of a Shostakovich quotation.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  13. Alex Ross — Unauthorized — The New Yorker, 30 August 2004 / 6 September print issue. Reports Testimony’s 1979 publication, Laurel Fay’s documentary challenge and the continuing distinction between corroborated anecdotes and authenticated authorship. Used as independent evidence of the controversy, not as a settled verdict on every memoir statement or on the finale’s meaning.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  14. Directive 2006/116/EC — copyright and related-rights terms — Article 1(1), ordinary life-plus-70 author term; Article 3, former 50-year phonogram/performer terms; Article 8, calculation from the following January; recital 17, relevant acts count regardless of country.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  15. Decca Eloquence — Artur Rodzinski, Complete Westminster Recordings — Label’s catalogue 4848489, CD 16: Shostakovich Symphony No. 5, Royal Philharmonic Orchestra. Quotes a High Fidelity review dated December 1955; that original review was subsequently located and visually inspected (source contemporary-review). The exact session ledger remains unavailable; inferred session fields are retained.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  16. High Fidelity — Shostakovich Fifth, Westminster 18001, December 1955 — Printed p. 80, PDF p. 82, first column, review signed A. F.; original scan visually inspected, with December 1955 footer confirmed on printed p. 67/PDF p. 69. Names Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London/Artur Rodzinski and explicitly identifies his second recording. Catalogue is printed SWN 18001, price $4.98 (or $3.98); work key is misprinted D major. Evidence of circulation by December 1955, not an exact first-release day.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  17. Directive 2011/77/EU — sound-recording term extension — Article 1(3), inserting Article 10(5): the extension applies to recordings still protected on 1 November 2013. A recording lawfully published by 1956 had exhausted the ordinary 50-year term before that extension.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
